cases.text:
Model Context Protocol servers are introducing new supply-chain risks through prompt injection and tool poisoning.

An AI agent executes what its tools dictate using its existing permissions. OX Security research found 834 flagged MCP servers where prompt injection or tool poisoning reached 22 percent. AWS confirmed and fixed CVE-2026-135614 where prompt injection made the Amazon ECS MCP Server return cleartext secrets. Langflow CVE-2026-105740 has seen 1,423 honeypot attempts since September. The poisoned tool does not need to execute code itself; it instructs the agent, which uses its own access.

- Upgrade Amazon ECS MCP Server to 0.1.36 or later and Langflow to 1.9.0 or later.
- Inventory MCP client configuration files like mcp.json and claude_desktop_config.json on developer and build hosts.
- Scope each MCP server to narrow credentials instead of personal tokens.
- Require human approval for agent tools that write, send, or delete.

https://theparijat.com/notes/2026-11-25-ai-spotlight-mcp-tool-supply-chain/

#CyberSecurity #CloudSecurity #ZeroTrust #AISecurity

cases.name: revised draft
cases.text:
An AI agent does what its tools tell it, with the permissions it already holds. That makes every MCP server it connects to part of its supply chain.

Three items this month:
- OX Security reviewed 834 flagged MCP servers and found prompt injection or tool poisoning in 22% of them. Flagged does not mean malicious.
- AWS fixed CVE-2026-135614: prompt injection could make the Amazon ECS MCP Server return cleartext secrets despite its redaction setting.
- Langflow CVE-2026-105740 runs commands defined in MCP server settings on the Langflow host. Honeypots have logged 1,423 attempts since September.

The poisoned tool does not need to run code. It instructs the agent, and the agent uses its own access. No step in that chain looks like malware.

What to do this week:
- Upgrade Amazon ECS MCP Server to 0.1.36 or later, then rotate any secret kept as a plaintext task-definition environment variable.
- Upgrade Langflow to 1.10.3 or later, keep authentication on, and keep it off the internet.
- Inventory MCP client configs (mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json) on developer and build hosts.
- Give each MCP server its own narrowly scoped credential, not a personal token.
- Require human approval for tools that write, send or delete.

Full write-up with framework mapping and hunting guidance:
https://theparijat.com/notes/2026-11-25-ai-spotlight-mcp-tool-supply-chain/

#AISecurity #MCP #PromptInjection #SupplyChainSecurity #CloudSecurity
